title: An injury is a change to their one goal; "also want" on top is an add that waits
origin: Spec #9 (step log and next step), cases 4 and 6: the coach decides which a request is

history.text: Yo Leo! 2 miles around the park at 6:30. You in?

plan.reason: Four runs a week builds the base without wrecking your legs.

testerLines: bad news, rolled my ankle on the run yesterday. doctor says no running for 6 weeks
could we do upper body stuff at home instead while it heals?
and separately I've been wanting to get my protein up too, like on top of the workouts
whatWentWrong: New case, not a past mistake: telling a change from an add.
shouldHaveHappened: The ankle is handled right away as a change to his one goal: sympathy without medical advice, then an adjusted exercise plan (upper body at home) worked out with him right away (shown or saved as a new version), never sent off to be thought about. The protein target on top is an add: a warm "let me think on it" with no promise and no nutrition questions or plan. ZOH never mentions a team, founders or approval.
